description: issue #685 (slice I6): `on_click` takes no argument (spec/interaction-events.md §Profile grammar: `on_click` takes none). A stray word where the block should be is not a block opener, so the reader reports a parse `ol-missing-end` pointed at the `on_click` head rather than silently accepting an argument. Because the parse fails, `execute()` bails before running anything, so no events are emitted and nothing is registered — and since issue #815 the check that runs beside the parse reports over the reader's RECOVERY AST too, in which the stray word ends the statement and `[ print "x" ]` reads as a list literal whose one element is a Command in value position. That third finding is a cascade of the first, not a separate defect in the program; it is recorded rather than suppressed because the rule that would suppress it is the precedence rule, which is scoped to an unresolvable CALLEE (`spec/execution-model.md:768-777`), and `on_click` resolves.

params.hint: wrap the body in [ ] or close it with end.
